example.name: Repository analysis SaaS
example.idea: Design the best architecture for a SaaS platform that analyzes GitHub repositories, finds security and quality problems and automatically proposes code improvements as pull requests.
example.goal: A production-ready MVP within three months that a team of three can operate.
example.requirements: EU data residency. Private repositories must never be used for model training. Budget for infrastructure below 1,000 EUR per month at launch.

documents.formats: PDF, Word (.docx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) up to 8 MB, images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) up to 3.5 MB, text files up to 200 kB; at most 10 per project. From PDF, Word and PowerPoint only the text is read. An image is described in text first – by an AI model of your choice or by you – and you confirm the description; the council reads only that text.
documents.imageIntro: The council reads this image only as text. Let a model describe it (one call on your own key, usually under 1 cent) or write the description yourself, check it and confirm it.
documents.descriptionBy: Description (draft by {model} – check and correct it)

repoLink.none: No repository linked. The Execution Council will start from an empty workspace.
repoLink.notLinked: The brief names {url}, but it is not linked: the CONSYRION AI GitHub App probably has no access to it. On GitHub open Settings → Applications → the CONSYRION AI app → Configure, add the repository, then click “Load repositories” and link it here. Without a link no pull request can be created.
repoLink.notConfigured: GitHub is not configured on this server.
repoLink.notInPlan: GitHub is not included in your plan. <link>See Billing & usage</link>.

repoContext.saved: Saved. Confirm the requirements again before the next council – the sources changed.
repoContext.saveError: Could not save the repository context
repoContext.intro: The models of a Decision council read the files you choose here, frozen at one commit, as context – not as requirements. Every model call reads them, so they add to the token use of a council.
repoContext.readable: {n, plural, one {# readable text file} other {# readable text files}}
repoContext.size: {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}, {size} ≈ {tokens} tokens per model call

suspicion.instruction: Reads like an instruction to the AI models (e.g. to ignore rules or to rate a proposal). The models never follow it.
suspicion.quoted_instruction: Quotes text that reads like an instruction to the AI models. If the product must handle this text as data (store, show, filter it), keep it – the models check it as a requirement and never follow the quoted text.
suspicion.meta_rule: Says when a requirement counts as met instead of describing the product. The council judges every proposal on substance; keep it only if it is a real product rule.

requirements.title: Hard requirements
requirements.intro: The council checks every proposal against exactly this list. Review it before the start – the number of sentences in the brief is no proof that nothing is missing.
requirements.changed: The brief or its documents changed after version {version} was confirmed (brief version {briefVersion}). Review the list and confirm it again before starting a council. Councils that already run keep the list they were started with.
requirements.confirmedNone: Confirmed: this brief has no hard requirements.
requirements.severalLimits: several limits – not checked as numbers
requirements.splitLimits: several limits in one sentence – split it to check each as a number
requirements.excludedSummary: {n, plural, one {# statement deliberately not taken over} other {# statements deliberately not taken over}}
requirements.sourceGone: source no longer in the brief
requirements.toDecideText: Nothing is kept or removed here on its own. Decide each statement before you confirm; the original wording stays unchanged.
requirements.excludedText: These statements from the brief or a document are not binding. Give a reason for each; they are shown to the council as excluded, so they do not come back as requirements.
requirements.reasonLabel: Reason for not taking it over
requirements.pendingImages: Confirm the description of {names} on the project page first – the council reads an image only through its confirmed description, so the requirements cannot be confirmed before.
requirements.unscanned: Not scanned for requirements (format): {names}. Add their hard requirements by hand.
requirements.notProposed: {n, plural, one {# further statement was not proposed because the list is full. Add it by hand if it is a requirement.} other {# further statements were not proposed because the list is full. Add the ones that are requirements by hand.}}
requirements.noHard: This brief has no hard requirements.
requirements.readOnly: Only members who can edit the project can confirm the requirements.
requirements.afterImplementationText: Before anything is built, no model can confirm “{text}”, so the council will end with “needs verification”. Keep it as it is, and add how it is measured (method, target value) so the proposals can be compared on it.
requirements.addPlan: Add a measurement plan as a requirement

voteWeights.title: Vote weights
voteWeights.intro: How much each model's scores and ranking count in the Final Verdict. Its own proposal is never weighted, and the feasibility check counts every model once. Fixed when the council starts.
voteWeights.sourceNote: Suggestions from the <link>{source}</link> (percentile tier 1–10). A model that is not in the ranking gets the neutral 5.

warning.dominant: {model} holds {share} % of the vote and outweighs all other models together.
warning.dominantTwo: {model} holds {share} % of the vote – at least twice the weight of {other}, so its evaluation mostly sets the ranking.

mode.title: 2. Decision mode
mode.independent_expert: Blind expert proposals with lighter structured feedback. Architecture, strategy, technology choice.
mode.adversarial_review: Deep 12 Minds scrutiny, rebuttals, two independent judges per objection. Security and high-stakes decisions.
mode.consensus: Several revision passes and an optional hybrid proposal. Dissent stays documented.

I accept that debate phases may be shortened to keep enough budget for the Final Verdict: if the budget runs short, Minority Review and Consensus Round are dropped and the proposals are not revised – the verdict then judges the first versions and is marked as shortened.
